items.quote: The suspect user account, "informant" (SID S-1-5-21-2425377081-3129163575-2985601102-1000, password hint "IAMAN"), was associated with the organizational email address iaman.informant@nist.gov.
items.why: Names the suspect account and the iaman.informant@nist.gov address, with evidence (carved address, Outlook profile/OST, the 'Resignation_Letter_(Iaman_Informant)' filename identifying Iaman Informant).

items.quote: a Windows 7 system running as a VMware virtual machine with hostname "informant-PC," network address 10.11.11.129
items.why: Windows 7 is identified, but the report never states the Ultimate edition, 64-bit, or the standalone WORKGROUP configuration.

items.quote: Removable Media 1 (cfreds_2015_data_leakage_rm1.E01), a USB flash drive formatted with exFAT, volume label "Authorized USB," serial number 5c75-4d3e
items.why: exFAT and the 'Authorized USB' label are right and backed by fsstat, but there is no SanDisk Cruzer Fit and no device serial 4C530012450531101593; the serial given is only the volume serial.

items.quote: Removable Media 2 (cfreds_2015_data_leakage_rm2.E01), a USB flash drive formatted with FAT, volume label "IAMAN $_@,"
items.why: The label is right, but the filesystem is only 'FAT' (not FAT32) and there is no SanDisk Cruzer Fit and no device serial 4C530012550531106501.

items.quote: Removable Media 3 (cfreds_2015_data_leakage_rm3_type3.E01), an optical disc (UDF write-once with VAT) labeled "IAMAN CD,"
items.why: The UDF optical disc is identified, but no format time is given (key Q33: formatted 2015-03-24 16:53:17 EDT = 20:53:17 UTC).

items.quote: Four documents matched exactly by file size between RM1 and RM2: [secret_project]_detailed_design.pptx matched winter_whether_advisory.zip at 16,381,123 bytes
items.why: Identifies the five Secret Project documents and shows by byte size that four of them reached USB RM2 under disguised names (consistent with Q53/Q56); however, it presents copying them onto RM1 as the exfiltration, which the key contradicts (scored under item 13).

items.quote: On RM2 and RM3, all 17 Office documents were renamed with false extensions in a deliberate anti-forensic concealment effort. The tsk.masquerade detection tool identified all 17 files by comparing the file extension against the actual content signature (OLE, DOCX, PPTX, or XLSX).
items.why: All 17 disguised files are listed with their true types and sizes, matching Q53, and supported by signature-mismatch evidence.

items.quote: Eraser was launched via its desktop shortcut at 15:12:28, and CCleaner64.exe followed at 15:15:50.
items.why: Both tools are shown downloaded, installed and run, with ShimCache, UserAssist, MFT and download-URL evidence; the times (11:12:28 and 11:15:50 EDT) match Q11/Q52.

items.quote: During March 23, the suspect conducted extensive web research demonstrating systematic preparation for the data theft operation. Search queries included "information leakage cases," "how to leak a secret," ... "anti-forensic tools" (85 URL hits carved from disk), "ccleaner" (65 hits), "eraser" (51 hits)
items.why: The leakage and anti-forensics searches are shown with carved-URL evidence, but some dates are wrong: per Q16, 'anti-forensic tools', 'eraser' and 'ccleaner' were searched on 2015-03-25 and 'security checkpoint cd-r' on 2015-03-24, not on March 23.

items.quote: Google Drive and iCloud Installed and Executed — Cloud Exfiltration Channels Prepared But No Confirmed Data Transfer
items.why: The Google Drive install and runs are shown (ShimCache, UserAssist, download at 15:56:33 EDT), but the report says the evidence 'prevents definitive classification as an exfiltration channel'; the key (Q30, Q59) shows files were uploaded and shared through it.

items.quote: Google Drive (googledrivesync.exe) was downloaded at 19:56:33 and iCloud (icloudsetup.exe) at 19:56:53, both from the NIST network (IP 129.6.58.42).
items.why: The icloudsetup.exe download on 2015-03-23 (~15:56 EDT) is shown with ShimCache/UserAssist evidence and treated as a further cloud channel.

items.quote: The E: drive (USB) was first detected on 2015-03-24 13:21:10, which coincides with the shellbag activity
items.why: No EVTX System-log USB events are given; the only connection time comes from MountedDevices and is wrong (Q22: first connected 2015-03-23 14:31:10 EDT; RM1 reconnected 03-24 09:38:00; RM2 09:58:32).

items.quote: The earliest exfiltration activity predates the suspect's PC by over a month. On February 15, 2015 at approximately 16:51–16:52 UTC, five secret project documents were copied to RM1 (the "Authorized USB" drive)
items.why: The key identifies RM1 as the company's authorized USB for confidential files (Sec. 2 fn 5, policy 1), from which the suspect copied files to the PC, so placing files on it is not exfiltration; the report itself says another computer did it, so attributing the copy to the suspect is unsupported.

items.quote: The browser history databases were successfully destroyed by CCleaner — no recoverable browser history files were found by the parse_browser_history tool.
items.why: Key Sec. 3 (2015-03-25 11:15): CCleaner was launched and then closed after doing nothing, and the Chrome/IE history is intact (Q14–Q16, Q44).

items.quote: The fact that ALL files are deleted indicates the device was intentionally wiped or formatted after the data exfiltration operation.
items.why: Deletion of every RM2 file is shown from FAT metadata, but the report gives no deletion time or 09:54–10:00 window (the key places the deletion as a quick format at ~17:02 EDT, Q54).

items.quote: Eleven embedded image SHA1 hashes matched identically across all three devices, and EXIF metadata signatures (Kodak DC260, Adobe Photoshop CS Macintosh) were consistent across all media.
items.why: RM3 is shown to hold the same 17 Secret Project documents as RM2, by exact sizes and embedded-image hashes, with their government-document content described.

items.quote: "winter_whether_advisory.zip" (MRU position 7 — accessed the masqueraded PPTX file)
items.why: Related evidence only: the report ties this access to the CD drive and assigns the E:\Secret Project Data shellbags to RM1; it never identifies winter_whether_advisory.zip as opened from RM2 (Q26: 10:01:23 EDT).

items.quote: The share was accessed first on 2015-03-22 (PC setup day) and again on 2015-03-23T20:23:28.
items.why: The traversed directories (Common Data, Past Projects, Secret Project Data subfolders, V:) match Q27 with shellbag evidence, but the first-access date is wrong: the key has the share first connected 2015-03-23 16:23 EDT, not 2015-03-22.
The report never mentions spy.conspirator@nist.gov or any e-mail exchange; it only notes that Outlook was used.

items.quote: Since FAT filesystems store local time, the offset is explained by the RM1 files having been written in a different timezone context (likely from the different source computer), not a discrepancy in the data.
items.why: Recognises that FAT stores local time but does not convert RM2's times: it labels the 09:54–10:00 / 09:59:27–10:00:18 copy times as UTC when they are EDT local (key: copy at 09:59 EDT = 13:59 UTC).

other_false_positives.quote: The complete data flow chain was: network share (10.11.11.128) to V: mapped drive to local staging directory ("S data" on Desktop) to USB RM1 (E:) to USB RM2 to optical disc RM3 (D:).
other_false_positives.why: Key Sec. 3 (2015-03-23 14:39, 2015-03-24 09:40) and Q22: files were copied from RM1 (the authorized company USB) to the PC; nothing went from 'S data' to RM1. The leak path was PC → RM2 → RM3, plus e-mail and cloud (Q59).

other_false_positives.quote: The suspect was able to connect personal USB devices (RM1 with volume label "Authorized USB" and RM2 with label "IAMAN $_@")
other_false_positives.why: Key Sec. 2 fn 5 and Sec. 1 policy (1): RM1 is the company's authorized USB memory stick holding confidential files, not a personal device.

other_false_positives.quote: The user "informant" (iaman.informant@nist.gov) possessed legitimate access to the workstation and the network file share as part of their organizational role at NIST.
other_false_positives.why: Key Sec. 1: Informant was a manager at the company OOO; NIST.gov is only the e-mail service used (Sec. 2 fn 4).

other_false_positives.quote: The informant account was created by IT administrators on March 22, 2015 as part of standard workstation provisioning.
other_false_positives.why: Key Sec. 3 ('Normal ~2015-03-22') lists the OS install and account creation as the suspect's own behaviour; the report gives no evidence of IT staff.

other_false_positives.quote: The suspect downloaded and executed Eraser 6.2.0.2962 and CCleaner 5.04 from the internet on the final day of activity, successfully destroying browser history databases and the local staging directory
other_false_positives.why: Key Sec. 3: 'S data' was deleted on 2015-03-24 10:07 with Shift+Delete; Eraser wiped \Desktop\temp on 03-25 (Q52) and CCleaner did nothing.

other_false_positives.quote: Twenty-two personal photographs were also placed on RM2 as visual cover content.
other_false_positives.why: Q53: the other files on RM2 'do not have a relationship with this scenario', and Sec. 3 has no cover-image step for RM2; the attribution is unsupported.

other_false_positives.quote: The masqueraded documents were first burned in directories with abbreviated names, then burned again with full directory names in subsequent sessions, and finally overwritten with three innocuous Windows sample photographs as the active session.
other_false_positives.why: Key Sec. 3 and Q33/Q57: at 16:54 the files were copied from RM2 with full directory names, the directories were renamed to abbreviations at 16:55, three meaningless files were added at 16:57 and the confidential files deleted at 16:58; there was no second burn with full names.

other_false_positives.quote: - Google Drive and iCloud installed (plausible deniability for cloud usage)
other_false_positives.why: Key Sec. 3 (16:32/16:38) and Q30/Q59: Google Drive was used to upload and share happy_holiday.jpg and do_u_wanna_build_a_snow_man.mp3 with the conspirator, not for deniability.

other_false_positives.quote: Block the Google account "informant" (identified from cookie "informant@accounts.google.com")
other_false_positives.why: Q31: the Google Drive account was iaman.informant.personal@gmail.com; this containment action targets an account the key does not support.

labelled_inferences_contradicted.quote: These appear to be genuine images that served as visual "cover" content on the USB device.
labelled_inferences_contradicted.why: Q53: the other RM2 files have no relationship with the scenario.

labelled_inferences_contradicted.quote: Cookie carved at disk offset 2664903014: "Cookie: informant@accounts.google.com/" — proves the user logged into Google services with a Google account named "informant"
labelled_inferences_contradicted.why: Q31: the Google account was iaman.informant.personal@gmail.com.

labelled_inferences_contradicted.quote: suggesting the user may have been verifying that their cloud-uploaded data was intact or accessing webmail to send the resignation letter
labelled_inferences_contradicted.why: Key Sec. 3 and Q52: at 11:22 EDT the suspect launched Google Drive to disconnect and sign out of the account; the letter was printed to XPS (Q37).

labelled_inferences_contradicted.quote: This is consistent with CCleaner execution at 2015-03-25 15:15:50, which was specifically designed to clear browser history, cookies, and cache.
labelled_inferences_contradicted.why: Key Sec. 3: CCleaner was closed after doing nothing; browser history is intact (Q14–Q16).

labelled_inferences_contradicted.quote: no direct evidence of document upload through these channels was recovered, likely due to the CCleaner execution that destroyed browser history and potentially sync logs
labelled_inferences_contradicted.why: Q30: sync_log.log survives and records the 16:32 uploads and 16:42 deletions; CCleaner did nothing.

labelled_inferences_contradicted.quote: The "S data" staging directory was also successfully deleted, as no trace remained in the MFT, likely through Eraser's secure deletion capability.
labelled_inferences_contradicted.why: Key Sec. 3: 'S data' was deleted on 2015-03-24 10:07 with Shift+Delete; Eraser wiped only \Desktop\temp on 03-25.

labelled_inferences_contradicted.quote: The USB device with the label "Authorized USB" specifically suggests an attempt to circumvent physical media policies.
labelled_inferences_contradicted.why: Key Sec. 2 fn 5: RM1 really is the company's authorized USB holding confidential files.
